source_batch.unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 4: Payment and Settlement Systems Act — Apply change-control notice and electronic-mode charge rules within their actual statutory scope

facts.statement: Courseware gives the prior-approval/participant-notice change process and section 10A prescribed electronic-mode charge prohibition. Its summary on p. 185 broadens the charge statement without repeating the prescribed-mode qualification.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 181–182, 185; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Section 11 ordinarily requires prior RBI approval and at least 30 days participant notice after approval for changes affecting structure/operation, with the stated RBI public-interest/monetary-policy proviso. Objection/comment steps do not replace approval. Section 10A concerns direct/indirect charges for modes prescribed under section 269SU, not all services regardless of scope.

payload.title: Build approval and notice into the change sequence
payload.core_explanation_md:
A change affecting a payment system's structure or operation ordinarily needs **prior RBI approval**, followed by at least 30 days' notice to participants under Section 11. The provision also has a specific RBI power to permit the stated notice variation in monetary-policy or public-interest circumstances.

Do not reverse the sequence by counting advance days before approval as though they necessarily satisfy post-approval notice. Nor should internal sign-off or a response to RBI objections be treated as the final approval itself. A release checklist should identify the applicable change, approval and notice evidence.

self_check.prompt_text: Which event precedes the ordinary participant-notice period under Section 11?
self_check.expected_takeaway: RBI approval precedes the specified notice to system participants.

payload.title: A scoped charge prohibition should not become an all-services rule
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 10A prohibits direct or indirect charges on persons making or receiving payments using the electronic modes prescribed under **Section 269SU** of the referenced tax legislation. Its scope depends on those prescribed modes.

A compliance review must identify the actual mode and the governing prescription. The courseware summary omits that scope qualification when broadly discussing charges; do not repeat it as a rule that every banking or payment service is free. Equally, relabelling a prohibited charge as indirect does not avoid the provision. Current mode prescriptions and any legislative cross-reference changes need verification before release.

self_check.prompt_text: What must be established before applying this particular charge prohibition?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Whether the payment uses a mode within the operative prescribed scope; indirect labels do not remove a covered charge.

payload.stem_md: A provider gives participants notice before requesting RBI approval for a structural change and assumes the pre-approval notice necessarily satisfies Section 11. What sequence needs checking?

options.text_md: Participant notice always replaces prior RBI approval
options.explanation_md: The section ordinarily requires both approval and the specified notice.

options.text_md: Internal project approval is identical to RBI approval
options.explanation_md: Internal governance cannot substitute for the statutory prior approval.

options.text_md: The provider may choose any notice exception without RBI involvement
options.explanation_md: The proviso concerns the specified RBI permission, not an exception invented by the provider.

options.text_md: Prior RBI approval followed by the ordinary post-approval participant notice
options.explanation_md: The statutory sequence and any valid variation must be established, not assumed from an earlier announcement.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The statutory sequence and any valid variation must be established, not assumed from an earlier announcement.

payload.stem_md: A training summary turns Section 10A into “all banking services must be free”. Which qualification is missing?

options.text_md: The rule applies only when a payer uses foreign banknotes
options.explanation_md: The provision concerns prescribed electronic payment modes, not a general foreign-cash condition.

options.text_md: Its scope is tied to the electronic modes prescribed under the referenced provision
options.explanation_md: A scoped electronic-mode rule cannot be expanded to every bank service without further authority.

options.text_md: Only charges with the word fee are covered
options.explanation_md: The text includes direct and indirect charges; the label alone is not decisive.

options.text_md: A bank may disregard the provision whenever a customer agrees
options.explanation_md: Customer agreement does not itself override the statutory prohibition where it applies.

payload.correct_explanation_md: A scoped electronic-mode rule cannot be expanded to every bank service without further authority.

payload.stem_md: RBI has objected to a proposed structural change. The provider sends comments and treats that reply as approval to launch. Which requirement remains?

options.text_md: Expiry of two weeks after sending comments, treated as automatic approval
options.explanation_md: The objection/comment periods do not create an automatic grant; the section still requires receipt of approval.

options.text_md: Approval by a majority of participants in place of RBI approval
options.explanation_md: Participant agreement does not replace the prior RBI approval required for the specified change.

options.text_md: Receipt of RBI approval before effecting the proposed change
options.explanation_md: The objection/comment exchange does not itself replace the approval required under Section 11.

options.text_md: Only evidence that the change improves customer convenience
options.explanation_md: A beneficial objective alone does not complete the approval process or override outstanding objections.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The objection/comment exchange does not itself replace the approval required under Section 11.
